talks.title: AI and Machine Learning in Network Security
talks.teaser: Discusses AI and Machine Learning in Network Security and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: A UC Santa Barbara professor and MixMode chief scientist presents at BSidesKC on AI and machine learning in network security, surveying first and second wave AI approaches.

Key Topics: The cybersecurity talent shortage of millions worldwide; compliance-focused data collection versus intelligent pattern extraction; first and second wave AI in security tools; and non-vendor-specific AI landscape assessment.

Technical Details: The speaker categorizes current security AI into first and second wave approaches, noting most tools focus on compliance data collection without underlying intelligence for pattern extraction at scale.

Takeaways: AI in network security remains early-stage despite marketing hype. Practitioners should understand AI wave distinctions and evaluate whether tools provide genuine intelligence or just faster data collection.

talks.title: The Monica Bellucci Fanclub - Detection and Defense Lessons Learned {...}
talks.teaser: Investigates the Monica Bellucci Fanclub - Detection and Defense Lessons Learned {...} and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Conti Forum Leak Context

Jason Gilliam of Huntress analyzes the Conti ransomware forum dump published after Ukraine's 2022 invasion by a researcher inside the group. He treats the leak as a public dataset for defensive lessons, not just ransomware trivia—Conti affiliates dispersed into other crews, spreading tradecraft rather than disappearing.

Parsing the Dump

Gilliam walks through his methodology for extracting actionable intelligence from messy, partially translated forum posts. He cautions about handling sensitive malware-laden archives but highlights value for detection engineers hunting pre-ransomware activity.

Tools and Techniques Observed

Forum discussions reference mainstream red-team tools—Cobalt Strike, Rubeus, Seatbelt, SharpChrome—alongside recon utilities like AdFind, AnyDesk, and Tor. He notes Conti guidance on avoiding password-lockout policies and using DClist/nltest for domain-controller discovery—commands rarely monitored despite being uncharacteristic for admins.

Detection Opportunities

The talk advocates correlating these precursors rather than focusing solely on encryption binaries. Simple rules combining nltest, DClist, and similar enumeration may catch intrusion stages that precede ransomware deployment across multiple successor groups.

talks.title: Mental Health Matters - You Are Not Alone
talks.teaser: Provides mental Health Matters - You Are Not Alone and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Mental health in security

The speaker reviews common conditions—bipolar disorder, depression, anxiety, ADHD—and prevalence data: about one in five US adults face a mental health condition yearly, one in seventeen a serious long-term illness, often diagnosed young.

Origins of Mental Health Hackers

CEO Amanda Berlin proposed a conference quiet space at DerbyCon 8 for anxiety and imposter syndrome; a GoFundMe raised $7,000, the group became an Ohio nonprofit in November 2018 and gained 501(c)(3) status in April 2019.

What the village provides

Villages offer inflatable loungers, coloring, yoga, free chair massages, stickers, and talks so attendees can decompress. Pre-COVID stats included $15,000 on massages, 20+ yoga hours, 2,000+ stickers, and 145 Slack volunteers. The semicolon motif represents choosing to continue after suicidal ideation.

talks.title: No Code Execution? No Problem! - Living The Age of Virtualization-Based Security
talks.teaser: Outlines no Code Execution? No Problem! - Living The Age of Virtualization-Based Security and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## Overview

Connor, a CrowdStrike software engineer, explains how Windows 11's default virtualization-based security (VBS) changes modern exploitation. The talk maps classic memory-corruption attack paths and shows how layered mitigations push attackers away from straightforward unsigned shellcode execution.

## From Shellcode to Kernel Constraints

Attackers traditionally write shellcode, mark memory executable, and run it. User-mode Arbitrary Code Guard (ACG) blocks writable-and-executable pages, but kernel protections require a kernel bug to disable ACG infrastructure. Connor walks through how these boundaries shape exploit development today.

## How VBS Works

VBS relies on a hypervisor that translates guest physical addresses to real host memory using extended page tables. Virtual machines never touch physical RAM directly; the hypervisor intercepts accesses and remaps them. Connor uses this model to explain why certain exploitation primitives become far harder when VBS features are enabled by default.

## Takeaways

The session is aimed at practitioners who want a clear mental model of Windows internals, not just a list of mitigations. Understanding VBS helps both offensive researchers and defenders reason about what still works when code execution is heavily restricted.
